Name: Agriculture: Cropland
Definition: Cells whose most common start-year annual NLCD class (30 m pixels in the model cell) is Cultivated Crops (82): annual crops, perennial woody crops and land being actively tilled.

Name: Agriculture: Pasture
Definition: Cells whose most common start-year annual NLCD class is Pasture/Hay (81): grasses or legumes planted for grazing or for seed or hay crops.

Name: Barren: All
Definition: Cells whose most common start-year annual NLCD class is Barren Land (31), and that are not forest in any year: bedrock, scree, sand, mines and other land with less than 15% vegetation.

Name: Developed: Open Space
Definition: Cells whose most common start-year annual NLCD class is Developed, Open Space (21): impervious surface under 20% of cover, mostly lawn grass, parks and large-lot housing.

Name: Developed: Low Intensity
Definition: Cells whose most common start-year annual NLCD class is Developed, Low Intensity (22): impervious surface 20-49% of cover.

Name: Developed: Medium Intensity
Definition: Cells whose most common start-year annual NLCD class is Developed, Medium Intensity (23): impervious surface 50-79% of cover.

Name: Developed: High Intensity
Definition: Cells whose most common start-year annual NLCD class is Developed, High Intensity (24): impervious surface 80-100% of cover.

Name: Developed: Transportation
Definition: Developed cells under a LANDFIRE road. Defined in the package's class list; the default Build does not map it.

Name: Forest: *
Definition: Cells that are forest (annual NLCD 41, 42 or 43) in any year of the record and are not developed, agricultural, water or ice in the start year, whose most common forest type among their 30 m pixels is the FIA forest type group "{*}". The type comes from the Build Options Forest Type Map: LANDFIRE EVT 2016 through the Land Cover Crosswalks (default), the USFS forest type group map, or TreeMap 2016. Forest cells with no typed pixel take their neighbours' type.

Name: Grassland: Annual
Definition: Start-year NLCD Shrub/Scrub (52) or Grassland/Herbaceous (71) cells that are never forest, whose most common RCMAP vegetation state (1985) is Annual Grassland (RCMAP value 2).

Name: Grassland: Natural Perennial
Definition: Start-year NLCD 52 or 71 cells that are never forest, whose most common RCMAP vegetation state (1985) is Natural Perennial Grassland (RCMAP value 3). Where RCMAP has no type (outside its western US extent), NLCD 71 cells.

Name: Grassland: Irrigated Perennial
Definition: Start-year NLCD 52 or 71 cells that are never forest, whose most common RCMAP vegetation state (1985) is Irrigated Perennial Grassland (RCMAP value 4).

Name: Shrubland: Native Sage Steppe
Definition: Start-year NLCD 52 or 71 cells that are never forest, whose most common RCMAP vegetation state (1985) is Native Sage Steppe (RCMAP value 5).

Name: Shrubland: Invaded Sage Steppe
Definition: Start-year NLCD 52 or 71 cells that are never forest, whose most common RCMAP vegetation state (1985) is Invaded Sage Steppe (RCMAP value 6).

Name: Shrubland: Sage
Definition: Start-year NLCD 52 or 71 cells that are never forest, whose most common RCMAP vegetation state (1985) is Sage Shrubland (RCMAP value 7).

Name: Shrubland: Non-sage
Definition: Start-year NLCD 52 or 71 cells that are never forest, whose most common RCMAP vegetation state (1985) is Non-sage Shrubland (RCMAP value 8). Where RCMAP has no type (outside its western US extent), NLCD 52 cells.

Name: Shrubland: Chaparral
Definition: Start-year NLCD 52 or 71 cells that are never forest, whose most common RCMAP vegetation state (1985) is Chaparral (RCMAP value 9).

Name: Snow/Ice: All
Definition: Cells whose most common start-year annual NLCD class is Perennial Ice/Snow (12).

Name: Water: All
Definition: Cells whose most common start-year annual NLCD class is Open Water (11).

Name: Wetland: Palustrine Forested
Definition: No cells at the start since 2026-11-10: palustrine woody wetland runs as the three forested wetland classes (to-do 53) and estuarine forested wetland as Wetland: Estuarine Forested. Kept so libraries and results made before then stay valid.

Name: Wetland: Spruce/Fir Group
Definition: Forested wetland of the Spruce/Fir group: palustrine woody wetland cells (start-year NLCD Woody Wetlands, 90, not estuarine in C-CAP 2001; or NLCD 95 that C-CAP maps as Palustrine Forested or Scrub/Shrub) whose forest type group is Spruce/Fir, plus woody wetland cells of other types in ecodivisions where this twin is most common among FIA hydric forest plots. Grows and decays on the group's FIA conditions on hydric sites (physiographic class 31-39).

Name: Wetland: Oak/Gum/Cypress Group
Definition: Forested wetland of the Oak/Gum/Cypress group: palustrine woody wetland cells (start-year NLCD Woody Wetlands, 90, not estuarine in C-CAP 2001; or NLCD 95 that C-CAP maps as Palustrine Forested or Scrub/Shrub) whose forest type group is Oak/Gum/Cypress, plus woody wetland cells of other types in ecodivisions where this twin is most common among FIA hydric forest plots. Grows and decays on the group's FIA conditions on hydric sites (physiographic class 31-39).

Name: Wetland: Elm/Ash/Cottonwood Group
Definition: Forested wetland of the Elm/Ash/Cottonwood group: palustrine woody wetland cells (start-year NLCD Woody Wetlands, 90, not estuarine in C-CAP 2001; or NLCD 95 that C-CAP maps as Palustrine Forested or Scrub/Shrub) whose forest type group is Elm/Ash/Cottonwood, plus woody wetland cells of other types in ecodivisions where this twin is most common among FIA hydric forest plots. Grows and decays on the group's FIA conditions on hydric sites (physiographic class 31-39).

Name: Wetland: Palustrine Emergent
Definition: Start-year NLCD Emergent Herbaceous Wetlands (95) cells whose most common C-CAP 2001 class is Palustrine Emergent Wetland (15), or that have no C-CAP wetland type.

Name: Wetland: Estuarine Forested
Definition: Estuarine forested wetland (mangroves, tidal swamps): start-year NLCD Woody Wetlands (90) or Emergent Herbaceous Wetlands (95) cells whose most common C-CAP 2001 class is Estuarine Forested (16) or Estuarine Scrub/Shrub Wetland (17), on its own generic forest curve and rates (the CONUS 1-km build's). Before 2026-11-10 these cells ran as Wetland: Palustrine Forested.

Name: Wetland: Estuarine Emergent
Definition: Start-year NLCD Emergent Herbaceous Wetlands (95) cells whose most common C-CAP 2001 class is Estuarine Emergent Wetland (18).

Name: Urbanization
Definition: Natural or agricultural cells that become developed: the cell's most common annual NLCD class changes to 21-24 from one year to the next.

Name: Intensification
Definition: Developed cells that move to a higher NLCD development intensity (21 to 22, 23 or 24; 22 to 23 or 24; 23 to 24).

Name: Ag Expansion
Definition: Natural cells that become agriculture: the cell's most common annual NLCD class changes to 81 or 82.

Name: Ag Change
Definition: Agricultural cells that change between pasture and cropland (the annual NLCD class goes from 81 to 82 or 82 to 81).

Name: Ag Contraction
Definition: Agricultural cells that stop being agriculture (the most common annual NLCD class leaves 81 or 82). Each cell returns to the nearest natural state class of the start year.

Name: Ag Contraction: Cropland
Definition: Ag Contraction from Agriculture: Cropland (NLCD 82).

Name: Ag Contraction: Pasture
Definition: Ag Contraction from Agriculture: Pasture (NLCD 81).

Name: Fire
Definition: Wildfire, by MTBS burn severity: low (MTBS 1 unburned to low and 2 low), medium (3 moderate) and high (4 high). The expected area per cell is the fraction of its 30 m pixels burned.

Name: Forest Harvest
Definition: Removal of trees by harvest, from LCMS Tree Removal: clearcut where last year's forest becomes shrub or grass in NLCD that year or within two years, selection where it stays forest.

Name: Mortality
Definition: High-severity tree mortality from drought, insects or disease: a stand that loses most of its live trees with no fire and no cutting (the western ecodivisions; mapped from LCMS stress classes and tree canopy loss).

Name: Restoration Wetland
Definition: Conversion of other land to wetland. Defined in the package's group list; no pathway uses it in the default model.

Name: Wetland Change: Gain
Definition: Gain of wetland area: water or barren land that becomes emergent wetland (USGS DSWE open water and the annual NLCD).

Name: Wetland Change: Loss
Definition: Wetland or barren land that becomes water, and water or emergent wetland that becomes barren (USGS DSWE open water and the annual NLCD).

Name: Urbanization: Open
Definition: A cell becomes Developed: Open Space (NLCD 21).

Name: Urbanization: Low
Definition: A cell becomes Developed: Low Intensity (NLCD 22).

Name: Urbanization: Medium
Definition: A cell becomes Developed: Medium Intensity (NLCD 23).

Name: Urbanization: High
Definition: A cell becomes Developed: High Intensity (NLCD 24).

Name: Intensification: Open to Low
Definition: Developed: Open Space becomes Developed: Low Intensity.

Name: Intensification: Open to Medium
Definition: Developed: Open Space becomes Developed: Medium Intensity.

Name: Intensification: Open to High
Definition: Developed: Open Space becomes Developed: High Intensity.

Name: Intensification: Low to Medium
Definition: Developed: Low Intensity becomes Developed: Medium Intensity.

Name: Intensification: Low to High
Definition: Developed: Low Intensity becomes Developed: High Intensity.

Name: Intensification: Medium to High
Definition: Developed: Medium Intensity becomes Developed: High Intensity.

Name: Ag Expansion: Cropland
Definition: A natural cell becomes Agriculture: Cropland (NLCD 82).

Name: Ag Expansion: Pasture
Definition: A natural cell becomes Agriculture: Pasture (NLCD 81).

Name: Ag Contraction Cropland: *
Definition: Agriculture: Cropland returns to the natural state class "{*}", the nearest natural class of the start year.

Name: Ag Contraction Pasture: *
Definition: Agriculture: Pasture returns to the natural state class "{*}", the nearest natural class of the start year.

Name: Fire: Low Severity
Definition: Wildfire of low severity: MTBS burn severity 1 (unburned to low) or 2 (low).

Name: Fire: Medium Severity
Definition: Wildfire of moderate severity: MTBS burn severity 3.

Name: Fire: High Severity
Definition: Wildfire of high severity: MTBS burn severity 4.

Name: Forest Harvest: Forest Clearcut
Definition: Stand-replacing harvest: LCMS Tree Removal on last year's forest that annual NLCD shows as shrub or grass that year or within two years.

Name: Forest Harvest: Forest Selection
Definition: Partial harvest: LCMS Tree Removal on last year's forest that stays forest.

Name: Forest Harvest: Forest Selection 20%
Definition: Light selection: a partial harvest removing 20% of live biomass (merchantable wood to the forestry sector, the rest to dead wood), with Forest Selection's minimum ages. No mapped source, so a zero target in the historical model; projections use it for the Forest Management page's lighter selection.

Name: Forest Harvest: Salvage Logging
Definition: Harvest of trees killed by a disturbance: on the disturbed forest classes only (wetland twins too), within 5 years of the disturbance, keeping the class and its age; it takes mostly snags to the forestry sector. It has no mapped source and a zero target in the historical model.

Name: Mortality: Drought and Insects
Definition: High-severity drought and insect mortality: about 83% of live tree carbon moves to snags, litter and dead roots and the cell goes to its Disturbed class.

Name: Restoration Wetland: *
Definition: Conversion to Wetland: {*}. Defined in the package's type list; no pathway uses it in the default model.

Name: Ag Change: *
Definition: Agricultural cells that change class: {*}.

Name: Wetland Change: *
Definition: Change among water, wetland and barren: the cell goes {*} (USGS DSWE open water and the annual NLCD; the two forested types have no pathway).

Name: Aquatic
Definition: Carbon moved out of the ecosystem to water bodies by lateral transport (a sink outside the ecosystem).

Name: Atmosphere
Definition: The atmosphere: the source of net growth and the sink of decay emissions (baseline flows).

Name: Atmosphere: CH4
Definition: Carbon emitted as methane by disturbance (transition-triggered flows only).

Name: Atmosphere: CO
Definition: Carbon emitted as carbon monoxide by disturbance (transition-triggered flows only).

Name: Atmosphere: CO2
Definition: Carbon emitted as carbon dioxide by disturbance (transition-triggered flows only).

Name: Biomass: Merchantable
Definition: Live carbon in merchantable stemwood (CBM-CFS3 merchantable pool).

Name: Biomass: Other Wood
Definition: Live carbon in branches, tops, stumps and non-merchantable trees (CBM-CFS3 other wood pool).

Name: Biomass: Foliage
Definition: Live carbon in foliage.

Name: Biomass: Coarse Root
Definition: Live carbon in roots 5 mm or more in diameter.

Name: Biomass: Fine Root
Definition: Live carbon in roots under 5 mm in diameter.

Name: DOM: Snag Stem
Definition: Dead organic matter: standing dead stemwood, from merchantable biomass turnover and mortality.

Name: DOM: Snag Branch
Definition: Dead organic matter: standing dead branches, from other wood turnover and mortality.

Name: DOM: Aboveground Very Fast
Definition: Dead organic matter: foliage and fine-root litter above the mineral soil (CBM-CFS3 AG very fast pool).

Name: DOM: Aboveground Fast
Definition: Dead organic matter: fine and small woody debris above the mineral soil (CBM-CFS3 AG fast pool).

Name: DOM: Aboveground Medium
Definition: Dead organic matter: coarse woody debris (down dead stems) (CBM-CFS3 medium pool).

Name: DOM: Aboveground Slow
Definition: Dead organic matter: humified organic horizons above the mineral soil (CBM-CFS3 AG slow pool).

Name: DOM: Belowground Very Fast
Definition: Dead organic matter: dead fine roots in the mineral soil (CBM-CFS3 BG very fast pool).

Name: DOM: Belowground Fast
Definition: Dead organic matter: dead coarse roots in the mineral soil (CBM-CFS3 BG fast pool).

Name: DOM: Belowground Slow
Definition: Dead organic matter: humified carbon in the mineral soil (CBM-CFS3 BG slow pool).

Name: Deep Soil
Definition: Stabilized soil carbon below the active mineral soil, fed from the belowground slow pool.

Name: DOM: Peat
Definition: Peat: the organic soil carbon a cell holds above its class's soil (gNATSGO soil above the class's, at most its Histosol share of it; stage 8). No decay of its own; lost to fire, to drainage under cropland and pasture, and to urbanization.

Name: DOM: Black Carbon
Definition: Dead organic matter: pyrogenic (black) carbon. Not used.

Name: Forestry Sector
Definition: Carbon removed from the ecosystem by harvest (transition-triggered flows only).

Name: Atmosphere
Definition: The Atmosphere stock types.

Name: Biomass: Aboveground
Definition: Live carbon above ground: merchantable, other wood and foliage.

Name: Biomass: Belowground
Definition: Live carbon below ground: coarse and fine roots.

Name: Biomass: Total
Definition: All live biomass carbon, above and below ground.

Name: DOM: Aboveground
Definition: Dead organic matter above the mineral soil.

Name: DOM: Belowground
Definition: Dead organic matter in the mineral soil.

Name: DOM: Deadwood
Definition: All dead wood: standing and down.

Name: DOM: Down Deadwood
Definition: Down dead wood as FIA measures it (CARBON_DOWN_DEAD): aboveground medium (down stems) and belowground fast (dead coarse roots).

Name: DOM: Litter
Definition: Forest floor as FIA measures it (CARBON_LITTER): aboveground very fast, fast and slow pools.

Name: DOM: No Soil
Definition: All dead organic matter except the mineral soil pools.

Name: DOM: Soil
Definition: Mineral soil carbon: belowground slow, belowground very fast and deep soil.

Name: DOM: Standing Deadwood
Definition: Standing dead wood: snag stems and snag branches.

Name: DOM: Total
Definition: All dead organic matter carbon.

Name: Total Ecosystem
Definition: All ecosystem carbon: biomass and dead organic matter.

Name: Net Growth Forest: *
Definition: Annual net uptake of carbon by forest into the live pool named after the arrow ({*}), from the fitted FIA growth curves.

Name: Net Growth Non Forest: *
Definition: Annual net uptake of carbon by grassland, shrubland and other non-forest classes into the live pool named after the arrow ({*}), from the package's non-forest rates.

Name: Net Growth Wetland Emergent: *
Definition: Annual net uptake of carbon by emergent wetland into the live pool named after the arrow ({*}).

Name: Biomass Turnover: *
Definition: Annual transfer of live biomass to dead organic matter by litterfall and natural mortality ({*}).

Name: Decay: *
Definition: Annual transfer of dead organic matter to a slower pool by decomposition ({*}).

Name: Emission: *
Definition: Annual release of carbon to the atmosphere by decomposition (heterotrophic respiration) ({*}).

Name: Transfer: *
Definition: Annual physical transfer between dead organic matter pools, such as snags falling ({*}).

Name: Stabilization: BG Slow -> Deep Soil
Definition: Annual transfer of mineral soil carbon to the stable deep soil pool.

Name: Lateral Transport: *
Definition: Annual loss of carbon to water bodies ({*}).

Name: LULC: Emission DOM CO2
Definition: Dead organic matter carbon emitted as CO2 by a disturbance or land-use transition.

Name: LULC: Emission DOM CO
Definition: Dead organic matter carbon emitted as CO by a disturbance or land-use transition.

Name: LULC: Emission DOM CH4
Definition: Dead organic matter carbon emitted as CH4 by a disturbance or land-use transition.

Name: LULC: Emission Live CO2
Definition: Live biomass carbon emitted as CO2 by a disturbance or land-use transition.

Name: LULC: Emission Live CO
Definition: Live biomass carbon emitted as CO by a disturbance or land-use transition.

Name: LULC: Emission Live CH4
Definition: Live biomass carbon emitted as CH4 by a disturbance or land-use transition.

Name: LULC: Harvest Live
Definition: Live biomass carbon removed to the forestry sector by harvest.

Name: LULC: Harvest DOM
Definition: Dead organic matter carbon removed to the forestry sector by harvest.

Name: LULC: Mortality Live
Definition: Live biomass carbon killed by a disturbance or land-use transition and moved to dead organic matter.

Name: LULC: Transfer DOM
Definition: Dead organic matter moved between pools by a disturbance or land-use transition.
The sum of the flow types in the group "{*}", in carbon (or carbon dioxide equivalent where the name says CO2e).

Primary stratum: the FIA ecological division "{*}" (ECOMAP 2007 divisions, dissolved; a Mountains division is the division's mountain provinces). Growth curves and carbon parameters vary by primary stratum.

Name: State: *
Definition: Secondary or tertiary stratum: the US state {*} (US Census TIGER/Line 2009).

Name: County: *
Definition: Secondary or tertiary stratum: the US county {*} (US Census TIGER/Line 2022).

Name: HUC6: *
Definition: Secondary or tertiary stratum: the watershed basin (hydrologic unit, 6-digit) {*} (USGS Watershed Boundary Dataset).

Name: HUC8: *
Definition: Secondary or tertiary stratum: the watershed subbasin (hydrologic unit, 8-digit) {*} (USGS Watershed Boundary Dataset).

Name: EPA L3: *
Definition: Secondary or tertiary stratum: the EPA Level III ecoregion {*}.

Name: Pyrome: *
Definition: Secondary or tertiary stratum: the pyrome {*}, a region of similar fire regime (Short and others, 2020).

Name: Federal: *
Definition: Secondary or tertiary stratum: fee land owned by {*} (PAD-US 4.0 owner; BIA = tribal land), or Non Federal.

Name: GAP: *
Definition: Secondary or tertiary stratum: PAD-US 4.0 GAP status {*} (the most protected status where designations overlap), or Not in PAD-US.

Name: Ecodivision: *
Definition: Secondary or tertiary stratum: the FIA ecological division {*} (ECOMAP 2007 divisions, dissolved).

Name: Agriculture Sector
Definition: Carbon removed from cropland and pasture each year by crop harvest and hay and grazing removal (a sink outside the ecosystem).

Name: Net Growth Agriculture: *
Definition: Annual uptake of carbon by cropland and pasture into the live pool named after the arrow ({*}): NASS county yields converted to growth with USDA Tech. Bull. 1939 Table 3-3 coefficients, varying by year through the Crop Yield flow multiplier.

Name: Harvest: Foliage -> Agriculture Sector
Definition: Crop harvest and hay and grazing removal: the harvested share of the year's aboveground growth, removed from the ecosystem.

Name: Disturbed: *
Definition: Land of the {*} after a stand-replacing disturbance (high-severity fire; moderate or high in shrubland), waiting either to return to it or to convert to non-forest or grassland. Age counts the years since the disturbance. No cell starts in it in the default Build (to-do 57).

Name: Post-disturbance: Forest Return
Definition: A disturbed forest class returns to its forest type, its age (years since the disturbance) carried over.

Name: Post-disturbance: Shrub Return
Definition: A disturbed shrub class returns to its shrub type, its age carried over.

Name: Post-disturbance: Conversion
Definition: A disturbed class that has not returned by the end of its window converts: disturbed forest to its ecodivision's shrub or grass class, disturbed sage, sage steppe and chaparral to annual grass, disturbed non-sage to its ecodivision's grass class.

Name: Post-disturbance
Definition: Every way out of a disturbed class: return or conversion.

Name: Post-disturbance: Forest Return
Definition: Return of disturbed forest to its forest type.

Name: Post-disturbance: Shrub Return
Definition: Return of disturbed shrubland to its shrub type.

Name: Post-disturbance: Conversion
Definition: Conversion of disturbed land that has not returned by the end of its window.

Name: Reforestation
Definition: Natural non-forest land (barren, shrub, grass or emergent wetland) that becomes forest with no fire or harvest behind it: slow recovery after a disturbance before the record, and encroachment onto land whose potential vegetation is not forest. Historical runs follow the annual NLCD (forest two years running); projections take the recent years' area and place it by a fitted surface (to-do 57).

Name: Reforestation: *
Definition: Natural non-forest land becomes the forest type "{*}", the type stage 5 gives the cell (its own, or its neighbours'); a new stand from age 0, the grass or shrub carbon carried over.

Name: Fuel Treatment: Mechanical Thinning
Definition: Fuel treatment by thinning from below (Fuel Treatments page): small trees and ladder fuels removed, merchantable wood to the forestry sector, slash treated. The forest type and stand age stay; for some years after, a wildfire in the cell is less often high severity (stage 9 multipliers by time since the treatment).

Name: Fuel Treatment: Prescribed Burn
Definition: Fuel treatment by prescribed underburning: litter and fine woody debris partly burned, some understory mortality. The forest type and stand age stay; for some years after, a wildfire in the cell is less often high severity.

Name: Fuel Treatment: Thin and Burn
Definition: Fuel treatment by thinning followed by prescribed burning: both carbon effects, and the strongest and longest reduction of high-severity fire.

Name: Fuel Treatment
Definition: Every fuel treatment: mechanical thinning, prescribed burn, thin and burn.

Name: Management: Replanting
Definition: Planting after a disturbance (Management Actions page): a disturbed forest class back to its forest type at age 0, without site preparation.

Name: Management: Replanting (failed)
Definition: A planting that did not take (the Management Actions page's survival): the cell stays in its disturbed class with its age, where it can still return or convert.

Name: Management: Replanting after Burn Site Prep
Definition: Planting after pile-and-burn site preparation (its carbon: the Site Preparation: Burn group).

Name: Management: Replanting after Burn Site Prep (failed)
Definition: A planting after pile-and-burn site preparation that did not take: the site preparation carbon flows, then the cell stays disturbed.

Name: Management: Replanting after Mechanical Site Prep
Definition: Planting after mechanical site preparation (mastication; its carbon: the Site Preparation: Mechanical group).

Name: Management: Replanting after Mechanical Site Prep (failed)
Definition: A planting after mechanical site preparation that did not take: the site preparation carbon flows, then the cell stays disturbed.

Name: Management: Replanting
Definition: Every replanting transition, planted or failed, with or without site preparation (to-do 58).

Name: Site Preparation: Burn
Definition: Replanting after pile-and-burn site preparation: shrub and herb cover burned, roots killed, half the litter and fine woody debris and 30% of the branch snags burned.

Name: Site Preparation: Mechanical
Definition: Replanting after mechanical site preparation (mastication): shrub and herb cover to litter and fine woody debris, roots killed.

Name: Management: Aerial Seeding
Definition: Post-fire aerial (broadcast) seeding of perennial grasses, forbs and sagebrush on burned sage and sage steppe (Management Actions page): a success goes to Native Sage Steppe at age 0.

Name: Management: Aerial Seeding (failed)
Definition: Aerial seeding that did not establish (the page's success share): the cell stays in its disturbed class with its age, where it can still return or convert.

Name: Management: Drill Seeding
Definition: Post-fire drill seeding of a native perennial grass mix (often with sagebrush broadcast) on burned sage and sage steppe: a success goes to Native Sage Steppe at age 0.

Name: Management: Drill Seeding (failed)
Definition: Drill seeding that did not establish: the cell stays disturbed with its age.

Name: Management: Sagebrush Planting
Definition: Planting sagebrush seedlings (plugs, container stock) on burned sage and sage steppe: a success goes to Native Sage Steppe at age 0.

Name: Management: Sagebrush Planting (failed)
Definition: Sagebrush planting that did not establish: the cell stays disturbed with its age.

Name: Management: Herbicide and Seeding
Definition: Pre-emergent herbicide against annual grass (imazapic or indaziflam) followed by seeding, on burned invaded steppe or converted annual grass in the Great Basin and steppe ecodivisions: a success goes to Native Sage Steppe at age 0.

Name: Management: Herbicide and Seeding (failed)
Definition: Herbicide and seeding that did not establish perennials: the cell stays in its class (burned invaded steppe or annual grass) with its age.

Name: Management: Rangeland Restoration
Definition: Every post-fire rangeland restoration transition, established or failed: aerial and drill seeding, sagebrush planting, herbicide and seeding.

Name: Emission: BG Slow -> Atmosphere (Wetland)
Definition: Annual release of soil carbon to the atmosphere as CO2 by decomposition in a wetland class: the part of the pool's emission that is not released as methane.

Name: Emission: BG Very Fast -> Atmosphere (Wetland)
Definition: Annual release of root litter carbon to the atmosphere as CO2 by decomposition in a wetland class: the part of the pool's emission that is not released as methane.

Name: Emission: AG Very Fast -> Atmosphere (Wetland)
Definition: Annual release of forest floor very fast litter carbon to the atmosphere as CO2 by decomposition in a wetland class: the part of the pool's emission that is not released as methane.

Name: Emission: AG Fast -> Atmosphere (Wetland)
Definition: Annual release of forest floor fast litter carbon to the atmosphere as CO2 by decomposition in a wetland class: the part of the pool's emission that is not released as methane.

Name: Emission: AG Slow -> Atmosphere (Wetland)
Definition: Annual release of forest floor slow litter carbon to the atmosphere as CO2 by decomposition in a wetland class: the part of the pool's emission that is not released as methane.

Name: Emission: BG Slow -> Atmosphere CH4
Definition: Annual release of soil carbon to the atmosphere as methane (CH4) in a wetland class, in carbon: the class's methane fraction of the pool's emission, set from a literature methane target and held at a cap (Carbon Assumptions: Wetland Methane).

Name: Emission: BG Very Fast -> Atmosphere CH4
Definition: Annual release of root litter carbon to the atmosphere as methane (CH4) in a wetland class, in carbon: the class's methane fraction of the pool's emission, set from a literature methane target and held at a cap (Carbon Assumptions: Wetland Methane).

Name: Emission: AG Very Fast -> Atmosphere CH4
Definition: Annual release of forest floor very fast litter carbon to the atmosphere as methane (CH4) in a wetland class, in carbon: the class's methane fraction of the pool's emission, set from a literature methane target and held at a cap (Carbon Assumptions: Wetland Methane).

Name: Emission: AG Fast -> Atmosphere CH4
Definition: Annual release of forest floor fast litter carbon to the atmosphere as methane (CH4) in a wetland class, in carbon: the class's methane fraction of the pool's emission, set from a literature methane target and held at a cap (Carbon Assumptions: Wetland Methane).

Name: Emission: AG Slow -> Atmosphere CH4
Definition: Annual release of forest floor slow litter carbon to the atmosphere as methane (CH4) in a wetland class, in carbon: the class's methane fraction of the pool's emission, set from a literature methane target and held at a cap (Carbon Assumptions: Wetland Methane).

Name: Emission: Wetland CH4
Definition: Methane released by wetland soil, root litter and (in forested wetlands) forest floor litter, in carbon. It is part of Emission: Total Rh.

Name: Emission: Wetland CH4 (CO2e)
Definition: Methane released by wetlands in carbon dioxide equivalent: Emission: Wetland CH4 times the CO2 equivalent of methane carbon (33.5 unless the Build set another value).

Name: Emission: Wetland Methane Source CO2
Definition: CO2 released by the wetland pools that also release methane, in carbon: the flows a marsh salinity or methane uncertainty multiplier adjusts to offset a change in methane.

Name: Q10 Wetland CH4
Definition: The wetland methane flows, grouped to carry their temperature response (Q10 2.57 unless the Build set another value). Not a quantity to report.

Name: Q10 Wetland Soil
Definition: The forested wetland soil CO2 flow, grouped to carry its temperature response (Q10 2.0 unless the Build set another value). Not a quantity to report.

Name: Emission Emergent: BG Slow -> Atmosphere
Definition: Annual release of soil carbon to the atmosphere as CO2 by decomposition in an emergent wetland: the part of the pool's emission that is not released as methane. It runs after the year's litter has reached the soil.

Name: Emission Emergent: BG Slow -> Atmosphere CH4
Definition: Annual release of soil carbon to the atmosphere as methane (CH4) in an emergent wetland, in carbon: the class's methane fraction of the pool's emission, set from a literature methane target and held at a cap (Carbon Assumptions: Wetland Methane). It runs after the year's litter has reached the soil.

Name: Emission Emergent: BG Very Fast -> Atmosphere
Definition: Annual release of root litter carbon to the atmosphere as CO2 by decomposition in an emergent wetland: the part of the pool's emission that is not released as methane.

Name: Emission Emergent: AG Very Fast -> Atmosphere
Definition: Annual release of aboveground litter carbon to the atmosphere as CO2 by decomposition in an emergent wetland.

Name: Decay Emergent: BG Very Fast -> BG Slow
Definition: Annual movement of root litter carbon into the soil in an emergent wetland.

Name: Q10 Wetland Flows
Definition: What an emergent wetland's litter and soil lose other than methane, soil export and burial, grouped to carry one temperature response (Q10 1.5 unless the Build set another value). Not a quantity to report.
